ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
A rectangular piece of paper $A B C D$ is $5 \mathrm{~cm}$ wide and $50 \mathrm{~cm}$ long. The paper is white on one side and grey on the other. Christina folds the strip as shown so that the vertex $B$ coincides with $M$ the midpoint of the edge $C D$. Then she folds it so that the vertex $D$ coincides with $N$ the midpoint of the edge $A B$. How big is the area of the visible white part in the diagram?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached figure is divided into three panels. In the first figure, a long rectangular strip is placed horizontally, A and D are at the left end, B and C are at the right end, and M is marked at the midpoint of the lower side CD; the dashed arc indicates folding the upper-right corner B to M, and the dashed slanted line indicates the first crease. In the second figure, the right end has already been folded into a gray folded part, B' is near the lower side, and C' is below; N is marked at the midpoint of the upper side AB, and there is a dashed arc indicating folding the lower-left corner D to N, with another left-side slanted crease. The third figure is the final state: the left and right ends each have a gray folded flap, and a visible white region remains in the middle. Reasoning: Model it using coordinate geometry. Let D=(0,0), C=(50,0), A=(0,5), B=(50,5). Since M is the midpoint of CD, M=(25,0); N is the midpoint of AB, so N=(25,5). The first fold makes B land on M, so the crease is the perpendicular bisector of BM. The midpoint of BM is (37.5,2.5), and the slope of BM is 1/5, so the slope of the crease is -5, and its equation is 5x+y=190. It intersects the upper side y=5 at P=(37,5), and the lower side y=0 at Q=(38,0). The right gray fold covers triangle MPQ within the middle region, whose area is 1/2 × 13 × 5 = 32.5. The second fold makes D land on N, so the crease is the perpendicular bisector of DN. The midpoint of DN is (12.5,2.5), and the slope of DN is 1/5, so the slope of the crease is also -5, and its equation is 5x+y=65. It intersects the upper side y=5 at S=(12,5), and the lower side y=0 at T=(13,0). The left gray fold covers triangle STN, whose area is likewise 1/2 × 13 × 5 = 32.5. For the white middle band between the two creases, when the height is 0≤y≤5, the right boundary is x=(190-y)/5, the left boundary is x=(65-y)/5, and the horizontal width is constantly 25, so the area is 25 × 5 = 125. The final visible white area is 125 - 32.5 - 32.5 = 60 square centimeters.

The first crease is the perpendicular bisector of BM, hence has equation 5x+y=190; it meets the top and bottom edges at P=(37,5) and Q=(38,0). The grey right fold covers the triangle with vertices M, P, Q inside the original strip, of area 32.5. The second crease is the perpendicular bisector of DN, equation 5x+y=65; it meets the top and bottom edges at S=(12,5) and T=(13,0). The grey left fold covers triangle S,T,N, also area 32.5.
